title: He didn’t come back slowly.
paragraphs: He didn’t come back slowly.

No pulse check.
No shallow breath.
No gradual awakening.
He stood up.

One moment—lifeless.
The next—alive, on his feet, inside a grave that was supposed to keep him.

“They threw the man into Elisha’s grave. And as soon as the man touched the bones of Elisha, he revived and stood on his feet.”
— 2 Kings 13:21
Pause.
Feel the weight of that.

This wasn’t a planned miracle.
No prophet speaking.
No crowd watching.
No worship music rising in the background.

Just fear.
Chaos.
A burial interrupted by raiders.
Men rushing.
A body thrown into the wrong grave.
And then—
Power.

Not from a heartbeat.
Not from a living hand.
From bones.
Dry. Silent. Buried bones.
Let that confront your theology.

God’s power did not expire when Elisha died.
It did not fade when the prophet was buried.
It did not weaken when the voice went silent.
Because it was never Elisha’s power.
It was always God’s.
And God does not decay.
Some of you are standing in the middle of something that feels buried.

A dream you once carried… now covered in dust.
A calling that used to burn… now feels cold.
A prayer you stopped praying… because nothing changed.
A version of you… you quietly declared “dead.”
You moved on.
You adjusted.
You learned to live with less faith, less fire, less expectation.
But this text refuses to let you settle.
Because God specializes in interrupting funerals.

This man didn’t even have faith recorded.
No prayer.
No repentance moment captured.
No dramatic cry to heaven.
Just contact.
He touched what God had once anointed…
…and life surged back.
Don’t miss it.

The miracle wasn’t in the bones.
The miracle was in the God who still honors what He has touched.

That’s the tension.
That’s the wonder.
And it points forward.
Because this is not the greatest resurrection story in Scripture.
This is a shadow.
A whisper.
A preview.

There is another tomb.
Another body laid down.
Another moment where it looked completely over.
But on the third day—
Jesus Christ didn’t wait for someone to touch Him.
He rose by His own power.
Not revived.
Resurrected.
Never to die again.

Elisha’s bones brought a man back temporarily.
Jesus’ empty tomb offers eternal life.
That’s the Gospel.
Let’s be honest.
We are that dead man.

Not physically.
Spiritually.
Ephesians 2:1 says we were dead in our trespasses and sins.

Dead in lust.
Dead in pride.
Dead in secret addictions.
Dead in hidden shame.
Dead in the version of ourselves we try so hard to hide from others.
Breathing… but not alive.
Functioning… but not free.
And then grace stepped in.

Not because we earned it.
Not because we cleaned ourselves up.
Not because we finally became “good enough.”
But because Jesus entered our grave.

He took our sin on the cross.
He absorbed the wrath we deserved.
He paid in full what we could never repay.
And then He rose.
So that anyone—anyone—who repents and believes in Him would not stay dead…
…but live.
Fully. Eternally. Unshakably.
So here’s the question.
What in your life have you already buried?

That relationship you gave up on?
That purity you think you can’t get back?
That calling you abandoned because of failure?
That intimacy with God you slowly walked away from?
You labeled it: “over.”
God says: “Watch Me.”
Because if He can bring life through bones…
If He can move power through a grave…
If He can reverse death without warning…
Then your situation is not beyond Him.
Not even close.
But don’t misunderstand the invitation.
This is not a call to chase miracles.
This is a call to come to Christ.
Because the goal is not temporary revival.
It is total resurrection.
Not just a better life.
A new life.
Jesus didn’t die so you could manage your sin.
He died so you could be freed from it.
He didn’t rise so you could stay the same.
He rose so you could become new.
Come honestly.

No filters.
No pretending.
No spiritual performance.

Bring the real you.
The tired you.
The guilty you.
The version of you that knows something is not right.
Lay it down.

Turn from sin.
Trust in Jesus alone.
And watch what only God can do.
Because when Christ touches what death has claimed…
death loses every time.

2 Kings 13:21
“He touched the bones… and stood on his feet.”
You’re not done.
God is not finished.
